Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Build, connect, and edit structures

Place water’s atoms, add its bonds, and build a reusable structure. Then connect pieces into methanol or edit a copy to make an ammonia model. Named attachment points let you refer to connection atoms without keeping track of their indices yourself.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.
Java imports 
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.molecule.*;
// Client code only:
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.*;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

Place the atoms and bonds of water

Atom indices start at zero. Every explicit atom, including H, must be supplied. Coordinates share one consistent length unit; the examples use ångströms for convenience. Choose explicit bonds to avoid distance-based guesses.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureFragment water() {
    // All atoms are explicit: StructureBuilder does not add hydrogens.
    return new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("O", 0, 0, 0)
        .atom("H", .7586, .5043, 0)
        .atom("H", -.7586, .5043, 0)
        .bond(0, 1)
        .bond(0, 2)
        .attachment("oxygen", 0)
        .atomConfiguration(0, new AtomicConfiguration(8, 8, 0, List.of(2, 6)))
        .atomConfiguration(1, new AtomicConfiguration(1, 0, 0, List.of(1)))
        .atomConfiguration(2, new AtomicConfiguration(1, 0, 0, List.of(1)))
        .build();
}

Place the atoms and bonds of water
Call Meaning Easy mistake
atom("O", x, y, z) Append an atom and return the builder Does not return its index; use addAtom for that
bond(0, 1) Single bond between existing atoms The second atom is index 1, not 2
attachment("oxygen", 0) A name for atom 0 Does not create a new atom or move it
build() Return a reusable fragment whose atoms and bonds cannot be changed in place Later edits work on copies
Place the atoms and bonds of water
JSON field / entry Meaning Easy mistake
atoms[] Each object adds one atom: e is its element symbol; x, y, z are its coordinates. Its array position is its zero-based index. Include every H atom in an explicit model; no implicit hydrogen is added.
bonds[] An entry [0,1] makes a single bond between atoms 0 and 1. An optional third entry selects the bond type. Omitting bonds enables distance inference; use an empty array for no bonds.
structure.attachments Map names to atom indices, for example {"oxygen":0} names atom 0. Move atoms and bonds inside structure too; do not mix it with top-level atoms/bonds.
The completed molecule object The loader validates and builds the definition when the file is loaded. There is no build field. The file path supplies the molecule ID.

Connect methyl and hydroxyl pieces into methanol

These pieces contain all the carbon, oxygen and hydrogen atoms of methanol. The code names a connection atom in each piece, appends copies, then adds a bond between those names. Making the bond does not move the pieces or remove any hydrogen: their coordinates and contents must already be suitable.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureFragment methyl() {
    return new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("C", 0, 0, 0)
        .atom("H", -.36, 1.03, 0)
        .atom("H", -.36, -.515, .892)
        .atom("H", -.36, -.515, -.892)
        .bond(0, 1)
        .bond(0, 2)
        .bond(0, 3)
        .attachment("carbon", 0)
        .build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static StructureFragment methyl() {
    return new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("C", 0, 0, 0)
        .atom("H", -.36, 1.03, 0)
        .atom("H", -.36, -.515, .892)
        .atom("H", -.36, -.515, -.892)
        .bond(0, 1)
        .bond(0, 2)
        .bond(0, 3)
        .attachment("carbon", 0)
        .build();
}

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureFragment hydroxyl() {
    // An open O site for assembly; this piece alone is not an alcohol.
    return new StructureBuilder()
        .atom("O", 1.43, 0, 0)
        .atom("H", 1.8, .85, 0)
        .bond(0, 1)
        .attachment("oxygen", 0)
        .build();
}

Assemble methanol in a separate helper

Keep the two fragment builders above. In Java, put the public classes in MethylFragment.java and HydroxylFragment.java, then put this helper in MethanolAssembly.java in the same package. Pass both fragments to join. The helper returns the finished geometry, which you can pass to your molecule builder. In scripts, call the helper after both fragment values are ready.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureFragment methanol() {
    // Fragment positions already line up. link() only adds the O–C bond.
    return StructureAssembly.builder()
        .part("methyl", methyl())
        .part("hydroxyl", hydroxyl())
        .link("methyl/carbon", "hydroxyl/oxygen", BondType.SINGLE)
        .build()
        .build(); // recipe first, then finite geometry
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static StructureFragment methanol() {
    // Fragment positions already line up. link() only adds the O–C bond.
    return StructureAssembly.builder()
        .part("methyl", methyl())
        .part("hydroxyl", hydroxyl())
        .link("methyl/carbon", "hydroxyl/oxygen", BondType.SINGLE)
        .build()
        .build(); // recipe first, then finite geometry
}
This operation runs in code. JSON stores definitions and recipes; it cannot call this method or handle events. Select or for the working example.
Expected result 6 atoms and 5 single bonds: CH4O. Attachments become methyl/carbon and hydroxyl/oxygen.
Tip A name identifies an atom, not a direction. Joining attachments adds the requested bond; it does not align pieces, remove H, fix valence, or optimize the shape. Duplicate names and unresolved paths are errors.

Edit a copy: water to an ammonia model

The code copies the water fragment, replaces oxygen with nitrogen, moves atoms, and adds a third hydrogen to make an ammonia display model. It returns new geometry; the original water is still usable. Replacing the element clears its old atom-specific nuclear data unless you supply new data.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureEditResult ammonia() {
    // Change O to N and add the third hydrogen: H2O -> NH3 as a graph edit.
    // This demonstrates authoring; it does not simulate a reaction.
    var editor = water()
        .edit()
        .replaceAtom(0, "N")
        .moveAtom(0, 0, 0, .25);
    int hydrogen = editor.addAtom("H", 0, -.85, -.35);
    return editor.setBond(0, hydrogen, BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static StructureEditResult ammonia() {
    // Change O to N and add the third hydrogen: H2O -> NH3 as a graph edit.
    // This demonstrates authoring; it does not simulate a reaction.
    def editor = water()
        .edit()
        .replaceAtom(0, "N")
        .moveAtom(0, 0, 0, .25);
    int hydrogen = editor.addAtom("H", 0, -.85, -.35);
    return editor.setBond(0, hydrogen, BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
}

Edit a copy: water to an ammonia model
Operation Index rule / result
Replace or move atom Uses the current geometry index; changing element clears its atom configuration
Create/replace/remove bond Use setBond or removeBond; no implied chemistry repair
Delete several atoms The whole selection resolves before deletion; surviving bonds, names, and overrides remap
Append a fragment Appends atoms and qualifies its names with the instance name
Finish editing build() returns the fragment plus original-to-final map; removed atoms map to -1
Edit a copy: water to an ammonia model
JSON edits entry Required fields Index rule / result
op: "replaceAtom" index, e Uses the current atom index; changing the element clears its old atomic configuration.
op: "moveAtom" index, x, y, z Moves one atom without changing its identity or bonds.
op: "setBond" / "removeBond" from, to; optional type for setBond Creates/replaces or removes one bond. No implied chemistry repair.
op: "removeAtoms" indices array Resolves the entire selection first, then remaps surviving bonds, names, and atomic data.
op: "append" instance, structure Appends the fragment and prefixes its attachment names with the instance name.
End of the edits array No extra finish field Edits run in array order on a copy. JSON does not expose the Java index-map result.

Read the index map after deleting atoms

Delete a group of atoms in one call when your selection uses their original numbers. The selection is resolved before anything is removed. Use the returned index map to find each surviving atom’s new number; removed atoms map to -1.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureEditResult isolateOxygen() {
    // Both selections refer to the ORIGINAL three-atom water fragment.
    // Deletion resolves the whole selection before removing any atoms.
    return water()
        .edit()
        .removeAtoms(1, 2)
        .build();
    // oldToNew() is [0, -1, -1]. The resulting O atom is not a water molecule.
}

public static StructureFragment water() {

        .atomConfiguration(2, new AtomicConfiguration(1, 0, 0, List.of(1)))
        .build();
}

Create hydrogen peroxide from a copy of water

This second example changes water into an H2O2 model. Its method names and sequential indices are the same ones used by JSON edits.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureEdits hydrogenPeroxideEdits() {
    // Water indices: O=0, H=1, H=2. Replace H=2 with O, then add its H.
    return StructureEdits.builder()
        .replaceAtom(2, "O")
        .moveAtom(2, -.9, -.95, 0)
        .atom("H", -1.65, -.6, .4)
        .setBond(2, 3, BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static StructureEdits hydrogenPeroxideEdits() {
    // Water indices: O=0, H=1, H=2. Replace H=2 with O, then add its H.
    return StructureEdits.builder()
        .replaceAtom(2, "O")
        .moveAtom(2, -.9, -.95, 0)
        .atom("H", -1.65, -.6, .4)
        .setBond(2, 3, BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
}

public static StructureFragment waterPair() {
    var water = water();
    // A disconnected pair of water molecules, not an inferred hydrogen bond.
    return water.qualified("first")
        .append("second",
            water.rotate(0, 0, 1, 180)
            .translate(3.2, 0, 0));
}

Move, rotate, and repeat a fragment
Tool Use it for
translate / rotate / scale / affine Return transformed copies. Rotate takes axis x/y/z plus degrees.
qualified("first") Give existing attachment names an instance prefix
instances(prefix, transforms) Make authored instances named prefix[0], prefix[1], …
group(name, assembly, transform) Place a nested collection as one unit
transformLast(matrix) Replace the last node’s transform; compose matrices yourself when combining transforms
Move, rotate, and repeat a fragment
JSON location / entry Use it for
structure.operations[] Ordered operations. Use op="translate" with by:[x,y,z], op="rotate" with axis and degrees, op="scale" with by, or op="affine" with matrix.
op: "append", instance: "first" Append the supplied structure and qualify its attachment names. There is no standalone qualified JSON operation.
op: "instances", prefix, transforms Place authored matrix copies named prefix[0], prefix[1], and so on.
Assembly node kind: "group", name, body, transform Place a nested assembly as one unit.
Assembly node transform A 3 × 4 authored matrix on that node; there is no transformLast field.

Close an 18-crown-6 ring

Six OCC units make the 18-membered ring. The author supplies the radius and rotation; the last link closes the open repeat boundary. This is a simple planar display model of C12H24O6, not its preferred conformation.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static StructureAssembly crownRing() {
    var unit = new StructureBuilder();
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        double angle = Math.toRadians(i * 20);
        double x = 4.4 * Math.cos(angle), y = 4.4 * Math.sin(angle);
        int atom = unit.addAtom(i == 0 ? "O" : "C", x, y, 0);
        if (i > 0) {
            int h1 = unit.addAtom("H", x, y, .95);
            int h2 = unit.addAtom("H", x, y, -.95);
            unit.bond(atom, h1)
                .bond(atom, h2);
        }
    }
    // Indices after H insertion: O=0, first C=1, second C=4.
    var fragment = unit.bond(0,
        1)
        .bond(1,
            4)
        .attachment("head",
            0)
        .attachment("tail",
            4)
        .build();
    double c = Math.cos(Math.PI / 3), s = Math.sin(Math.PI / 3);
    double[][] turn = {
        {
            c,-s,0,0
        }, {
            s,c,0,0
        }, {
            0,0,1,0
        }
    };
    return StructureAssembly.builder()
        .repeat("ring", StructureAssembly.builder()
            .part("unit", fragment)
            .build(), 6, turn)
        .neighbor("unit/tail", "unit/head", 1, BondType.SINGLE)
    // Neighbor links leave the boundary open; this closes it explicitly.
        .link("ring[last]/unit/tail", "ring[first]/unit/head", BondType.SINGLE)
        .build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.molecule.BondType

def molecules = mods.avogadro.molecules
def molecule = molecules.builder("guide:crown")
molecule.name("18-crown-6")
def assembly1 = molecules.assemblyBuilder()
def assembly2 = molecules.assemblyBuilder()
def fragment3 = molecules.structureBuilder()
fragment3.atom("O", 4.4, 0.0, 0.0)
fragment3.atom("C", 4.134647531457998, 1.5048886306329425, 0.0)
fragment3.atom("H", 4.134647531457998, 1.5048886306329425, 0.95)
fragment3.atom("H", 4.134647531457998, 1.5048886306329425, -0.95)
fragment3.atom("C", 3.3705955497235034, 2.828265482620773, 0.0)
fragment3.atom("H", 3.3705955497235034, 2.828265482620773, 0.95)
fragment3.atom("H", 3.3705955497235034, 2.828265482620773, -0.95)
fragment3.bond(1, 2, BondType.SINGLE)
fragment3.bond(1, 3, BondType.SINGLE)
fragment3.bond(4, 5, BondType.SINGLE)
fragment3.bond(4, 6, BondType.SINGLE)
fragment3.bond(0, 1, BondType.SINGLE)
fragment3.bond(1, 4, BondType.SINGLE)
fragment3.attachment("head", 0)
fragment3.attachment("tail", 4)
def geometry4 = fragment3.build()
assembly2.part("unit", geometry4)
def geometryRecipe5 = assembly2.build()
assembly1.repeat("ring",
    geometryRecipe5,
    6,
    [[0.5000000000000001,
        -0.8660254037844386,
        0.0,
        0.0] as double[],
        [0.8660254037844386,
            0.5000000000000001,
            0.0,
            0.0] as double[],
        [0.0,
            0.0,
            1.0,
            0.0] as double[]] as double[][])
assembly1.neighbor("unit/tail", "unit/head", 1, BondType.SINGLE)
assembly1.link("ring[last]/unit/tail", "ring[first]/unit/head", BondType.SINGLE)
def geometryRecipe6 = assembly1.build()
molecule.structure(geometryRecipe6)
molecules.register(molecule)

In a molecule file, put the assembly recipe inside structure.assembly.

Repeat a connected row of carbon atoms

This places a carbon fragment three times and joins the copies using the connections you specify. Use this pattern for repeated structures. The result has three connected carbon sites; it is an intentionally incomplete chemistry example, with no added hydrogens or inferred reactions. 

var cell = new StructureBuilder()
    .atom("C", 0, 0, 0)
    .cell(new double[][] {
        {
            1.42, 0, 0
        }
    })
    .link(0, 0, new int[] {
        1
    })
    .build();
var chain = cell.repeat(new int[] {
    3
}, new boolean[] {
    false
});
var moved = chain.translate(2, 0, 0)
    .rotate(0, 0, 1, 90);

val cell = Avogadro.fragment {
    atom("C", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    cell(arrayOf(doubleArrayOf(1.42, 0.0, 0.0)))
    link(0, 0, intArrayOf(1))
}
val chain = cell.repeat(intArrayOf(3), booleanArrayOf(false))
val moved = chain.translate(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    .rotate(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 90.0)

def cell = molecules.structure {
    atom('C', 0d, 0d, 0d)
    cell([[1.42d, 0d, 0d]] as double[][])
    link(0, 0, [1] as int[])
}
def chain = cell.repeat([3] as int[], [false] as boolean[])
def moved = chain.translate(2d, 0d, 0d)
    .rotate(0d, 0d, 1d, 90d)

val cell = Avogadro.fragment { b =>
  b.atom("C", 0, 0, 0)
      .cell(Array(Array(1.42, 0.0, 0.0)))
      .link(0, 0, Array(1))
}
val chain = cell.repeat(Array(3), Array(false))
val moved = chain.translate(2, 0, 0)
      .rotate(0, 0, 1, 90)

val cell = Molecules.fragment()
    .atom("C", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    .cell([[1.42, 0.0, 0.0]])
    .link(0, 0, [1], "SINGLE")
    .build();
val chain = cell.repeat([3], [false]);
val moved = chain.translate(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    .rotate(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 90.0);
Molecules.molecule("my_pack:chain")
    .geometry(moved)
    .register();

Transforms return new geometry. Repeat counts and wrap flags have one entry per cell vector. Wrap true connects periodic boundaries without moving coordinates. Cell expansion, affine transforms, append, qualification and cylinder wrapping use the same bounds and topology validation in ZenScript as in Java. See the structures guide for complete operation rules.

Wrap a strip around a cylinder

The four points move from the X axis onto a cylinder around the Y axis. The circumference is 12 coordinate units. The existing bonds follow the points.

Edit a copy and keep the original structure

The example changes a copy while leaving the original fragment available. Atom numbers start at zero. Each operation uses the numbers after the preceding operation, so deletion can change which number refers to an atom. The returned map gives the final number for each original atom, or -1 if it was removed. 

var hydroxyl = new StructureBuilder()
    .atom("O", 0, 0, 0)
    .atom("H", 0.96, 0, 0)
    .bond(0, 1)
    .attachment("oxygen", 0)
    .build();
var result = hydroxyl.edit()
    .moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0, 0)
    .removeAtom(1)
    .build();
int oxygenNow = result.remap(0);
int removedHydrogen = result.remap(1);
var edited = result.fragment();

val hydroxyl = Avogadro.fragment {
    atom("O", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    atom("H", 0.96, 0.0, 0.0)
    bond(0, 1);
    attachment("oxygen", 0)
}
val result = Avogadro.edit(hydroxyl) {
    moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0.0, 0.0);
    removeAtom(1)
}
val oxygenNow = result.remap(0)
val removedHydrogen = result.remap(1)
val edited = result.fragment()

def hydroxyl = molecules.structure {
    atom('O', 0d, 0d, 0d);
    atom('H', 0.96d, 0d, 0d)
    bond(0, 1);
    attachment('oxygen', 0)
}
def result = molecules.edit(hydroxyl) {
    moveAtom(1, 0.97d, 0d, 0d);
    removeAtom(1)
}
def oxygenNow = result.remap(0)
def removedHydrogen = result.remap(1)
def edited = result.fragment()

val hydroxyl = Avogadro.fragment { b =>
  b.atom("O", 0, 0, 0)
      .atom("H", 0.96, 0, 0)
      .bond(0, 1)
      .attachment("oxygen", 0)
}
val result = Avogadro.edit(hydroxyl) { edit =>
  edit.moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0, 0)
      .removeAtom(1)
}
val oxygenNow = result.remap(0)
val removedHydrogen = result.remap(1)
val edited = result.fragment()

val hydroxyl = Molecules.fragment()
    .atom("O", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    .atom("H", 0.96, 0.0, 0.0)
    .bond(0, 1, 1)
    .attachment("oxygen", 0)
    .build();
val result = hydroxyl.edit()
    .moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0.0, 0.0)
    .removeAtoms([1])
    .build();
val oxygenNow = result.remap(0);
val removedHydrogen = result.remap(1);
val edited = result.geometry;

Bulk removal resolves its whole selection before remapping. Replacing an element clears incompatible atom-specific overrides. Materialize a unit cell or network preview before topology editing. No edit guesses missing bonds, caps or valence repair.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or setting Arguments What it does
StructureBuilder.atom(element, x, y, z) Element symbol; position Add each atom explicitly in a consistent coordinate unit.
bond(first, second) Zero-based atom indices Connect two atoms already present in the builder.
attachment(name, atomIndex) Reusable name; existing atom index Expose a connection point for assembly.
atomConfiguration(index, configuration) Atom index; nuclear/electron data Attach the inspection data you want displayed.
build() No arguments Return the completed fragment for reuse or registration.

When you finish: A builder creates a model but does not add it to the game. Java registrations use a name, called an owner, to group the definitions your mod controls; choose your mod ID. A RegistrationJob lets you cancel pending work or remove its installed set later. JSON and Groovy registrations use their file or script loading rules instead. Keep drawing and exports in client code.
